Play out a full Skat game

Source: R/game.R
sk_play_game.Rd

Plays all ten tricks of a Skat game given the three players' hands, the declared game type, and which player is declarer. The two non-declarers form the defending team. Bidding is assumed already resolved; this simulates the card play and scores the result.

Usage

sk_play_game(
  hands,
  skat,
  declarer,
  game_type,
  players = NULL,
  game_value = NULL,
  hand_game = FALSE,
  call = rlang::caller_env(),
  schneider_announced = FALSE,
  schwarz_announced = FALSE,
  ouvert = FALSE
)

Arguments

hands

A length-3 list of sk_card vectors (ten cards each), as from sk_deal().

skat

An sk_card vector of length 2 (the skat). Its points are credited to the declarer in suit and grand games, including hand games.

declarer

Integer in 1:3: the declaring player.

game_type

A single game-type string, one of sk_game_types().

players

A length-3 list of sk_player objects, one per seat. Defaults to heuristic players for all seats.

game_value

Optional complete scoring value. If NULL (default), it is computed from the original hand plus skat and achieved/announced levels. This is not a bid; overbidding must be resolved by the caller.

hand_game

Logical; whether the skat was left untouched. Defaults to FALSE.

call

The calling environment, used for error reporting.

schneider_announced, schwarz_announced

Logical announcements, valid only for suit/grand hand games. Failure to achieve the level loses the game.

ouvert

Logical; open play. Suit/grand ouvert implies hand and both announcements and requires every trick; null ouvert still requires no trick.

Value

An object of class sk_game: a list with elements

  • result: an sk_result object from sk_score_game(),

  • tricks: a length-10 list, each element a list of cards, leader, winner, and points,

  • declarer: the declaring seat,

  • game_type: the game type played,

  • declarer_points: the integer card points credited to the declarer, trick points plus skat points, including hand games – the same total the result was scored on,

  • tricks_won: the integer number of tricks the declarer took.

See also

sk_simulate() to repeat this over many deals, and sk_solve_dd() for exact double-dummy analysis of an endgame.

Examples

d <- sk_deal(seed = 42)
g <- sk_play_game(d$hands, d$skat, declarer = 1, game_type = "grand")
g$result$won
#> [1] FALSE
g$declarer_points
#> [1] 25
